subject: POC: Success criteria & KPI follow-up
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlaspayments.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: POC: Success criteria & KPI follow-up

Hi Samantha / Raj —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can kick off the POC next week: please confirm owners and timelines below.

Recap (from today's discovery)
- Primary use case: real-time transaction classification and fraud signal enrichment for processor pipeline.
- Target throughput: ~peak 50 req/s with bursts to 100 req/s during batch windows.
- Latency requirements: P95 under 200ms (end-to-end inference).
- Cost sensitivity: target cost/token <= $0.0005 (we'll optimize via batching & quantization).
- Quality bar: classification accuracy >= 92% on your labeled holdout; F1 > 0.90 for fraud class.

Proposed POC success criteria (please confirm):
1) Latency: P95 inference latency <= 200ms on sample production-like traffic (50 req/s).
2) Throughput: Sustained 50 req/s with <2% error rate; burst to 100 req/s for 5 minutes.
3) Cost: Average cost per token <= $0.0005 across the evaluation window.
4) Quality: Accuracy >= 92% on your labeled test set and no regressions from baseline ruleset.
5) Stability: No more than 1 incident requiring manual restart during the 2-week trial.

Evaluation plan (attached): redwood-poc-eval-plan-20261005.csv — defines datasets, measurement windows, and who will run the load tests.
Owners / timeline (proposed):
- Atlas: Samantha (technical lead) / Raj (product) — provide labeled holdout + access to sample traffic by 2026-10-09.
- Redwood: Jordan (POC delivery), Marissa (CS & quality monitoring), Rishi (commercial/contracting).
- Kickoff: 2026-10-12 (provisioning + smoke test).
- Evaluation window: 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-26 (2 weeks).

Next steps:
- Samantha: confirm owners and the dataset access cadence.
- Raj: confirm procurement timeline for SOW / procurement items we shared.
- Redwood: we'll provision a dedicated POC endpoint and share measurement dashboards + DocuSign SOW draft.

Attachment: redwood-poc-eval-plan-20261005.csv (CSV)
Attachment: initial-POC-notes.txt (TXT)

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

--

Thanks Rishi — this all looks good and aligned with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the SOW: 

- For throughput: when you say "sustained 50 req/s" can you confirm whether that is concurrent but asynchronous single-token queries or multi-turn conversations? We will provide a mix of small (single-step) and medium (3-5 turn) interactions.
- For cost/token measurement: we need details on what tokens baseline you'll use (e.g., model tokenizer, tokenization rules) so finance can sanity-check the estimate.

Also: we'll add a short quality rubric — how we count "accuracy" for borderline cases and how we handle label disagreements. Can Marissa own the quality monitoring side?

Procurement note: procurement wants the SOW and an estimated monthly spend baseline before routing to legal. Raj, can you share your procurement timeline?

Looping Marissa in to own quality monitoring & evaluation during the POC. Suggested changes and next steps from our side: 

1) Throughput nuance: we'll define two traffic profiles in the eval plan: (A) single-turn (avg. tokens 16) and (B) multi-turn (avg. tokens 60). We'll validate sustained 50 req/s under profile A and burst test profile B up to 100 req/s.
2) Token accounting: Redwood will use the model tokenizer (BPE) as the measurement baseline and will provide a tokenization report for the sample datasets so finance can compute cost/token.
3) Quality rubric: Marissa will set up acceptance tests and a small adjudication flow for label disagreements (3-person review).
4) Instrumentation: we'll provide a dashboard (link below) with P95, P99, error rates, tokens-per-request, and cost estimates sampled daily.

Proposed timeline update:
- 10/09: Atlas to share sample holdout & traffic snapshot.
- 10/12: Kickoff + provisioning (smoke tests).
- 10/13 - 10/26: Evaluation window (2 weeks).
- 10/27: Review meeting + go/no-go decision.

I've attached a short POC checklist for Marissa and the onboarding playbook. Marissa — can you confirm you can run acceptance criteria and the adjudication flow?

Thanks all — quick confirmation and next actions: 

- Samantha: appreciate the throughput clarification; we'll run both profiles (A and B) as Jordan outlined.
- Marissa: confirmed to own quality monitoring and adjudication flow.
- Raj: pending procurement timeline; we'll attach the SOW draft for review.

Finalized success criteria for the POC (agreed):
- Latency: P95 inference latency <= 200ms (profile A baseline).
- Throughput: sustained 50 req/s for profile A; burst to 100 req/s for profile B for up to 5 minutes with <2% error rate.
- Cost: measured using Redwood token accounting (BPE tokenizer) with target average cost/token <= $0.0005 across evaluation window.
- Quality: Accuracy >= 92% on Atlas labeled holdout; adjudication process for disputed labels with >2 reviewers for edge cases.
- Stability: zero manual restart incidents for critical endpoint (target), but acceptance allows <=1 incident during trial.

We uploaded the SOW draft and the final evaluation plan to the shared Drive and attached the SOW locally for convenience. DocuSign link will follow once Raj confirms procurement details.

Attachments: POC-SOW-Atlas-20261012.pdf (PDF), redwood-poc-eval-plan-20261005.csv (CSV)
